summary: Crop Helper transforms 40+ years of NASA Earth data into precise planting and rotation decisions, mitigating climate risks and securing credit approval. Operating in Sergipe, Brazil today, its global satellite architecture is built to scale across any agricultural frontier in the world.
details:
Planting decisions in climate-vulnerable drylands cannot afford to be a gamble. Today, agronomists, extensionists, and agricultural advisors face a critical dilemma: extreme climate volatility, unpredictable El Niño cycles, and strict regulatory windows that dictate farm credit and insurance approval. Missing the planting window costs entire harvests.

Crop Helper eliminates this uncertainty. It is an intelligent decision-support platform that transforms complex Earth telemetry into field-level agronomic prescriptions.

How do we solve it? We fuse 40+ years of NASA Earth observation data (rain, evapotranspiration, terrain) with official agronomic calendars (ZARC) and yield records. In seconds, Crop Helper calculates localized drought risks, verifies planting windows, and prescribes resilient intercropping and rotation strategies across crops like maize, beans, and cassava.

Today, Crop Helper is active across Sergipe, Brazil—a rigorous proving ground bridging Semi-arid and Agreste extremes. But this is just the launchpad: because our engine runs on global NASA satellite telemetry, Crop Helper is designed to scale anywhere in the world, adapting planting decisions across any agricultural frontier.

We replace guesswork with deterministic geospatial intelligence. Crop Helper secures credit eligibility, mitigates climate shocks, and empowers technical leaders to guide resilient harvests with absolute confidence.
